content: Dr. Ahmad Tibi, born on December 19, 1958, is an Israeli Arab politician and the leader of the Arab nationalist party Ta'al (the Arab Movement for Renewal). He was elected to the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, on a joint ticket with the United Arab List. Dr. Tibi identifies himself as Arab-Palestinian by nationality but has referred to Israel as his homeland and has pledged to remain in Israel regardless of the political future of the Palestinian territories. He hails from Taibeh, located in the Center District of Israel. Dr. Tibi is a trained physician and graduated from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. During his medical career, Dr. Tibi worked as a resident at Hadassah Hospital, which is known for fostering positive Jewish-Arab relations. However, these relations were tested when an incident occurred in which Dr. Tibi struck a security guard on the head with his briefcase, causing an injury that required stitches. He left the scene while the guard was bleeding. Dr. Tibi was dismissed from his position a few hours later. He contested his dismissal, claiming it was due to his Arab identity and arguing that the guard should have shown more respect to a doctor. The hospital, on the other hand, stated that Dr. Tibi had refused to allow his briefcase to be searched, and the security guard was simply performing his duties. Dr. Tibi also has a notable political career. He served as a political advisor to the late Palestinian Authority Chairman Yasser Arafat for several years and even represented the Palestinians during the 1998 Wye River negotiations. In 1999, he resigned from his advisory role to run for the Knesset. Dr. Tibi has described his relationship with Arafat as close and extremely interesting and important. He was first elected to the Knesset in 1999 as a member of Azmi Bishara's Balad party but later broke away to form his own party, Ta'al, during the same Knesset session. In 2002, right-wing Knesset member Michael Kleiner initiated efforts to restrict Dr. Tibi's movements within the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, accusing him of aiding Palestinians in their conflict against Israel. Dr. Tibi challenged these restrictions, arguing that they were unconstitutional and illegal under Israeli law. He appealed to the Supreme Court of Israel, which deferred its decision on the matter. Ahead of the 2003 Israeli elections, several right-wing politicians, including leaders of the National Union and National Religious Party, sought to disqualify Dr. Tibi from running for Knesset office. Likud MK Michael Eitan officially filed a motion to disqualify Dr. Tibi's candidacy, which narrowly passed the Israeli Central Elections Committee by one vote. Eitan accused Dr. Tibi of supporting Palestinian terrorism during the intifada, serving as an advisor to Yasser Arafat, and exploiting his parliamentary immunity to advance Palestinian interests. Eitan also alleged that Dr. Tibi had engaged in anti-Israeli activities, including incitement, sedition, and expressing solidarity with Israel's adversaries. However, the Supreme Court of Israel unanimously overturned the ban, allowing Dr. Tibi to run for office. He was subsequently elected as part of a joint list of Ta'al and Hadash. Before the 2006 elections, Dr. Tibi withdrew his Ta'al party from the Hadash coalition and joined the United Arab List. He currently serves as a Deputy Speaker of the Knesset.
